hook.text: Ribosomes, DNA, and ion channels all work below 100 nanometers — cells run on nanomachinery.

buildup.text: Nanoparticles match the size of biological molecules, letting them interact with cells directly.

discovery.text: When nanoparticles enter the body, proteins coat them within seconds, forming a 'corona.'

twist.text: The protein corona — not the bare particle — decides if the immune system attacks or ignores it.

climax.text: Researchers engineer corona formation to slip nanoparticles past defenses and reach tumors.

punchline.text: At the nanoscale, biology and engineering merge.

quiz.question: What is the 'protein corona' on a nanoparticle?
options: A protective polymer shell added during manufacturing
A layer of proteins that adsorbs onto the nanoparticle in the body
A corona-shaped nanoparticle used in vaccines
